title: Routing overlay precedence causing eval entropy shifts from sampling defaults and termination normalization
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Customer reported reproducible eval quality regressions after the runtime change that normalized termination tokens and introduced a per-route sampling defaults overlay. The regression appears in Hosted and Private pools for a subset of customers running strict JSON eval suites; outputs contain trailing fragments or extra tokens, causing failed matches and metric drops. This ticket coordinates investigation, mitigations, and the planned hotfix across routing, runtime config precedence, and private pool deploys.
impact: High — two enterprise customers reported failing evals on critical prompt sets used in production. Automated guardrails flagged increases in false-positive token outputs across 3 benchmark suites; customer-facing SLAs at risk.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use customer prompt set A (JSON strict) with model:open-compat-1 at hosted region us-west-2
2) Send batched requests with per-request sampling unspecified (rely on route defaults)
3) Observe extra trailing tokens in ~12% of responses vs baseline (prior to config change)
4) Repeat same prompt against a Dedicated/private pool with identical model and runtime version; reproduce failure when route overlay exists
investigation_notes: 2026-02-25: Initial triage by oncall. Noticed correlation between rollout of 'route-level sampling overlay' (runtime-1.21) and spike in JSON eval failures.
2026-02-26: Reproduced locally with a synthetic harness; variation appears only when route overlay is present and per-request sampling params omitted.

2026-03-01: Tokenization differences in private pools amplify the effect — suffix whitespace normalization in routing layer removed explicit end-of-sequence markers from canonical termination lists for some languages.
2026-03-04: Found precedence bug: route overlay applied after termination-normalization step, so normalized termination list could be overwritten by an empty fallback in private pool configs.
2026-03-08: Verified fix branch locally that changes overlay application order; early tests reduce failed JSON evals to baseline.
root_cause: A config precedence bug introduced in runtime-1.21: the route-level sampling overlay was applied after the termination-normalization pass, causing an unintended emptying of per-route termination token lists when private pool config overlays were present. This allowed sampling defaults to favor higher-entropy generation and dropped explicit stop markers for some tokenization variants, leading to trailing fragments in strict evals.
mitigation: 1) Roll back route-level overlay for affected customers in hosted control plane (completed for customer A on 2026-03-03). 2) Apply per-customer emergency override that pins termination lists to pre-change canonical values for private pools. 3) Deploy runtime safety toggle that preserves pre-normalization termination lists when overlay is unset.
resolution_plan: Short-term (hotfix): Cherry-pick overlay-order fix into runtime-1.21-hotfix branch and deploy to hosted control plane + private package. Target runtime rollout: 2026-03-15.

Medium-term: Add a config validation check in control plane to prevent empty termination lists after overlays are applied; add integration test that runs customer's strict eval suites during canary rollouts.
Long-term: Improve telemetry surface — per-route termination coverage and sampling entropy delta metric in Console; automatic regression alert when strict-eval pass rate drops >5% post-deploy.
customer_communications: 2026-02-26: Notified Customer A and Customer B that we are investigating changes correlated with their eval regressions.
2026-03-03: Informed Customer A that we rolled back route overlay for their org as mitigation; asked for verification runs.
2026-03-09: Sent detailed technical summary and planned hotfix ETA to Customer B; scheduled joint validation window for 2026-03-16.
